chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Bureyd al-Ijaly, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who set out as a pilgrim, and with him was a camel of his, and expense money, and provisions. So he died on the way. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was Sarurah (one who had not yet performed the obligatory Hajj), then died in Ihram, then the Hajj of Al-Islam suffices for him. And if he died while he was Sarurah before he entered into Ihram, his camel and his provisions and his expenses and whatever was with him are made to be for the Hajj of Al-Islam. So if there is something excess from that, then it is for the inheritors, if there are no debts upon him.'

I said, 'What is your view if the Hajj was optional (Nafl), then he died on the way before he entered into Ihram, for whom would be his camel, and his expense money, and whatever was with him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'All that was with him and whatever he left would be for the inheritors, except if there are debts upon him, so they are paid off on his behalf; or if he had bequeathed a bequest, so that bequest is executed for the one to whom he bequeathed it, and that is taken from his one-third.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.صَرُورَة: One who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj

ai.seo_question: What happens to a pilgrim's wealth if he dies before or after entering Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential distinction between dying in the state of Ihram versus before it, determining whether the Hajj obligation is fulfilled or if assets are liquidated for inheritance. It establishes that if the Hajj was obligatory, the pilgrim's wealth covers the cost of a substitute performing Hajj on his behalf, while optional Hajj assets revert fully to heirs after debts and bequests. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the financial continuity of religious duties and the precise allocation of estate assets for posthumous worship.
